verses.text: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
Until the day when He was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, He had given commandments to the apostles whom He had chosen.
After His passion (suffering and death), He showed Himself alive to them by many infallible proofs (sure signs). They saw Him for 40 days, and He spoke about the things of the kingdom of God.
When He was gathered together with them, He commanded them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father. He said: You have heard about this from Me.
For John truly baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.
So when they had come together, they asked Him: Lord, will You at this time restore (give back) the kingdom to Israel?
He said to them: It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father has put in His own power.
But you will receive power after the Holy Spirit has come upon you. And you will be witnesses unto Me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and to the farthest part of the earth.
When He had spoken these things, while they watched, He was taken up. And a cloud received Him out of their sight.
While they looked steadfastly (kept staring) toward heaven as He went up, two men stood by them in white clothes.
They said: Men of Galilee, why do you stand gazing up into heaven? This same Jesus, who is taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you have seen Him go into heaven.
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet (the Mount of Olives), which is a sabbath day's journey (a short walk, about 1 mile) from Jerusalem.

When they came in, they went up into an upper room. Staying there were Peter, James, John, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon Zelotes (the Zealot), and Judas the brother of James.
These all continued with one accord (all agreeing together) in prayer and supplication (asking God), with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
In those days Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples and spoke. The number of people together was about 120.
Men and brothers, this scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke before by the mouth of David about Judas, who was the guide for those who took (arrested) Jesus.
For he was numbered (counted) with us, and had a part in this ministry (work).
Now this man bought a field with the reward of iniquity (money paid for his sin). And falling headlong, he burst open in the middle, and all his bowels (insides) gushed out.
This was known to all the people living at Jerusalem. So that field is called in their own language Aceldama, which means The field of blood.
For it is written in the book of Psalms: Let his home be desolate (empty), and let no man live in it. And: Let another take his bishoprick (his office).
So, of these men who have been with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
Beginning from the baptism of John to that same day when He was taken up from us, one must be ordained (chosen) to be a witness with us of His resurrection (rising from the dead).
They appointed (put forward) 2 men: Joseph called Barsabas, who was also named Justus, and Matthias.
They prayed and said: You, Lord, who know the hearts of all men, show which of these 2 You have chosen,
To take the part of this ministry (work) and apostleship, from which Judas fell by transgression (sin), so that he might go to his own place.
Then they cast their lots (a way of choosing), and the lot fell on Matthias. And he was numbered (counted) with the 11 apostles.

verses.text: When the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all with one accord (all agreeing together) in one place.
Suddenly there came a sound from heaven like a rushing, mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
There appeared to them tongues split apart, like fire, and it sat upon each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other tongues (languages), as the Spirit gave them the words to say.
There were living at Jerusalem Jews, devout (God-fearing) men, out of every nation under heaven.
When this was noised abroad (when people heard about it), the crowd came together and were confounded (confused), because every man heard them speak in his own language.
They were all amazed and marveled (wondered), saying to one another: Look, are not all these who speak from Galilee?
How then do we each hear them in our own language, the language we were born with?
Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people living in Mesopotamia, in Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
Phrygia and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya near Cyrene, and visitors from Rome, Jews and proselytes (people who became Jews),
Cretes and Arabians, we hear them speak in our own languages the wonderful works of God.
They were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying to one another: What does this mean?
Others mocking said: These men are full of new wine.
But Peter, standing up with the 11, lifted up his voice and said to them: Men of Judea, and all you who live at Jerusalem, know this, and listen to my words.
For these men are not drunk, as you suppose (think), since it is only the third hour of the day (9 in the morning).
But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel:

And it will come to pass in the last days, says God, I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh (all people). Your sons and your daughters will prophesy (speak God's message), your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
And on My servants and on My handmaidens (women servants) I will pour out My Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy (speak God's message).
I will show wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth below: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke.
The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable (glorious) day of the Lord comes.
And it will come to pass that whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth was a man approved (shown to be true) by God among you by miracles, wonders, and signs, which God did by Him in the middle of you, as you yourselves also know.
Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel (set plan) and foreknowledge of God, you have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and killed.
God raised Him up, having loosed (freed Him from) the pains of death, because it was not possible that He should be held by it.
For David speaks about Him: I saw the Lord always before my face. For He is at my right hand, so that I should not be moved.
So my heart rejoiced, and my tongue was glad. Also my flesh (body) will rest in hope,
Because You will not leave my soul in hell (the grave), and You will not let Your Holy One see corruption (decay).
You have made known to me the ways of life. You will make me full of joy with Your presence.
Men and brothers, let me speak freely to you about the patriarch (father of the nation) David. He is both dead and buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
So being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that from the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, He would raise up Christ to sit on his throne,
David, seeing this before, spoke about the resurrection (rising from the dead) of Christ, that His soul was not left in hell (the grave), and His flesh (body) did not see corruption (decay).
This Jesus God has raised up, and we are all witnesses of it.
So being lifted up by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, He has poured out this, which you now see and hear.
For David has not gone up into the heavens. But he says himself: The LORD said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand,
Until I make Your enemies Your footstool.
So let all the house of Israel know for sure that God has made that same Jesus, whom you have crucified, both Lord and Christ.
When they heard this, they were pricked (deeply hurt) in their heart, and said to Peter and to the rest of the apostles: Men and brothers, what shall we do?

Then Peter said to them: Repent (change your heart), and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ because of the remission (forgiveness) of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God will call.
With many other words he testified (told the truth) and exhorted (urged) them, saying: Save yourselves from this untoward (crooked) generation.
Then those who gladly received his word were baptized. And the same day about 3,000 souls (people) were added to them.
They continued steadfastly (kept on faithfully) in the apostles' doctrine (teaching) and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
Fear came upon every soul (person), and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles.
All who believed were together, and had all things common (shared everything).
They sold their possessions and goods, and parted (gave) them to all men, as every man had need.
They continued daily with one accord (all agreeing together) in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house. They ate their food with gladness and singleness (sincerity) of heart,
Praising God, and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily those who should be saved.

verses.text: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour (3 in the afternoon).

A certain man who was lame from his mother's womb (from birth) was carried there. They laid him daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms (gifts of money) from those who went into the temple.
He saw Peter and John about to go into the temple, and asked for alms (a gift of money).
Peter, fastening his eyes on him with John, said: Look on us.
He gave heed (paid attention) to them, expecting to receive something from them.
Then Peter said: Silver and gold I have none, but what I have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk.
He took him by the right hand and lifted him up. And right away his feet and ankle bones received strength.
Leaping up, he stood and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They knew that it was he who sat for alms (gifts of money) at the Beautiful gate of the temple. And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
As the lame man who was healed held Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the porch called Solomon's, greatly wondering.

When Peter saw it, he answered the people: Men of Israel, why do you marvel (wonder) at this? Or why do you look so earnestly (hard) at us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man walk?

The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His Son Jesus, whom you delivered up, and denied Him in the presence of Pilate, when Pilate had decided to let Him go.
But you denied the Holy One and the Just (Righteous One), and asked for a murderer to be given to you,
And killed the Prince of life, whom God has raised from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
His name, through faith in His name, has made this man strong, whom you see and know. Yes, the faith which is by Him has given him this perfect soundness (complete healing) in front of you all.
And now, brothers, I know that you did it through ignorance (not knowing), as your rulers also did.
But those things which God had shown before by the mouth of all His prophets, that Christ should suffer, He has fulfilled in this way.
So repent (change your heart), and be converted (turn to God), so that your sins may be blotted out (wiped away), when the times of refreshing will come from the presence of the Lord.
He will send Jesus Christ, who before was preached to you,
Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution (restoring) of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began.
For Moses truly said to the fathers: A Prophet the Lord your God will raise up to you from your brothers, like me. You must hear Him in all things, whatever He says to you.
And it will come to pass that every soul (person) who will not hear that Prophet will be destroyed from among the people.
Yes, and all the prophets from Samuel and those who came after, as many as have spoken, have also told about these days.
You are the children of the prophets, and of the agreement which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham: And in your seed (family line) all the families of the earth will be blessed.
To you first God, having raised up His Son Jesus, sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities (sins).

verses.text: As they spoke to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them,
Being grieved (upset) that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection (rising) from the dead.
They laid hands on them, and put them in hold (jail) until the next day, for it was now evening.
But many of those who heard the word believed. And the number of the men was about 5,000.
On the next day, their rulers, elders, and scribes (teachers of the law),
And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and as many as were of the family of the high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem.
When they had set them in the middle, they asked: By what power, or by what name, have you done this?
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: You rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
If we this day are examined about the good deed done to the weak man, by what means he is made whole (healed),

Be it known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by Him this man stands here in front of you whole (healed).
This is the stone which was set at nought (thrown away as worthless) by you builders, which has become the head of the corner (the most important stone).
Neither is there salvation in any other. For there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.

When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and saw that they were unlearned and ignorant (not trained in schools) men, they marveled (wondered). And they took knowledge (noticed) that they had been with Jesus.
Seeing the man who was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they talked among themselves,
Saying: What shall we do to these men? For truly a notable (clear) miracle has been done by them, and it is plain to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us strictly threaten them, that from now on they speak to no man in this name.
They called them, and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered them: Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you more than to God, you judge.
For we cannot help but speak the things which we have seen and heard.
So when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding nothing to punish them for, because of the people. For all men glorified God for what was done.
For the man on whom this miracle of healing was shown was more than 40 years old.
Being let go, they went to their own company (friends), and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
When they heard that, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord (all agreeing together), and said: Lord, You are God, who has made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all that is in them.
You said by the mouth of Your servant David: Why did the heathen (nations) rage, and the people imagine vain (useless) things?
The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against His Christ.
For truly against Your holy child Jesus, whom You have anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) and the people of Israel, were gathered together,
To do whatever Your hand and Your counsel (plan) determined before to be done.
And now, Lord, look on their threatenings, and grant (give) to Your servants that with all boldness they may speak Your word,
By stretching out Your hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of Your holy child Jesus.
When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered together was shaken. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.
The crowd of those who believed were of one heart and of one soul. Not one of them said that any of the things he owned was his own, but they had all things common (shared everything).
With great power the apostles gave witness of the resurrection (rising from the dead) of the Lord Jesus. And great grace was upon them all.
There was no one among them who lacked (needed anything). For as many as owned lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,
And laid them down at the apostles' feet. And it was given to every man as he had need.
Joses, who was surnamed (also named) Barnabas by the apostles, which means The son of consolation (comfort), a Levite, and from the country of Cyprus,
Having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet.

verses.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession (some land).
Ananias kept back part of the price. His wife also knew about it. He brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet.
But Peter said: Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
While it remained, was it not your own? And after it was sold, was it not in your own power? Why have you thought of this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God.
Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and gave up the ghost (died). And great fear came on all those who heard these things.
The young men got up, wound him up (wrapped his body), carried him out, and buried him.
About 3 hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter answered her: Tell me whether you sold the land for so much. She said: Yes, for so much.

Then Peter said to her: How is it that you have agreed together to tempt (test) the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.
Then right away Sapphira fell down at Peter's feet, and gave up the ghost (died). The young men came in and found her dead. They carried her out and buried her by her husband.
Great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things.
By the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders done among the people. And they were all with one accord (all agreeing together) in Solomon's porch.
Of the rest, no man dared to join himself to them. But the people magnified (praised) them.
Believers were added to the Lord more and more, crowds of both men and women.
So they brought the sick out into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, so that at least the shadow of Peter passing by might fall on some of them.
Also a crowd came out of the cities around to Jerusalem. They brought sick people, and those who were vexed (troubled) with unclean spirits. And every one of them was healed.
Then the high priest rose up, and all who were with him, which is the sect (group) of the Sadducees. They were filled with indignation (anger),
And laid their hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.
But the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night, brought them out, and said:
Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

When they heard that, they entered into the temple early in the morning, and taught. But the high priest came, and those who were with him. They called the council together, and all the senate (elders) of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have the apostles brought.
But when the officers came, and did not find the apostles in the prison, they went back and told,
Saying: The prison truly we found shut with all safety, and the keepers standing outside before the doors. But when we had opened, we found no man inside.
When the high priest, the captain of the temple, and the chief priests heard these things, they doubted (wondered) what this would grow into.
Then one came and told them, saying: Look, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people.
Then the captain went with the officers, and brought the apostles without violence. For they feared the people, that they might be stoned.
When they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the high priest asked them,
Saying: Did we not strictly command you that you should not teach in this name? And look, you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine (teaching), and intend to bring this man's blood upon us.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said: We ought to obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed and hanged on a tree.
God has exalted (lifted up) Jesus with His right hand to be a Prince and a Savior, to give repentance (a change of heart) to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.
And we are His witnesses of these things. And so is also the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.
When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and took counsel (made plans) to kill the apostles.
Then a Pharisee in the council stood up, named Gamaliel, a doctor (teacher) of the law, who was honored among all the people. He commanded them to put the apostles outside for a little while.
Gamaliel said to them: Men of Israel, take heed (be careful) about what you plan to do with these men.

For before these days Theudas rose up, boasting himself to be somebody. A number of men, about 400, joined themselves to him. He was killed, and all who obeyed him were scattered, and brought to nothing.

After this man, Judas of Galilee rose up in the days of the taxing (the count of the people), and drew away much people after him. He also perished (died), and all, even as many as obeyed him, were scattered.
And now I say to you: Stay away from these men, and let them alone. For if this counsel (plan) or this work is of men, it will come to nothing.
But if it is of God, you cannot overthrow it. Or else you may be found even to fight against God.
They agreed with Gamaliel. When they had called the apostles, and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
The apostles left the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.
Daily in the temple, and in every house, they did not stop teaching and preaching Jesus Christ.

verses.text: In those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied (growing), there arose a murmuring (complaining) of the Grecians (Greek-speaking Jews) against the Hebrews. They complained because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration (giving out of food).
Then the 12 called the crowd of the disciples to them, and said: It is not reason (not right) that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.
So, brothers, look among you for 7 men of honest report (good name), full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry (work) of the word.

This saying pleased the whole crowd. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte (a man who became a Jew) of Antioch.
They set these men before the apostles. When the apostles had prayed, they laid their hands on them.
The word of God increased. And the number of the disciples in Jerusalem multiplied (grew) greatly. And a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people.

Then some from the synagogue (meeting house) arose, which is called the synagogue of the Libertines (freed slaves), and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and some of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing (arguing) with Stephen.
They were not able to resist (stand against) the wisdom and the Spirit by which Stephen spoke.
Then they secretly got men to say: We have heard him speak blasphemous words (words against God) against Moses, and against God.
They stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes (teachers of the law). They came upon Stephen, caught him, and brought him to the council.
They set up false witnesses, who said: This man does not stop speaking blasphemous words (words against God) against this holy place and the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place, and will change the customs which Moses delivered (gave) to us.
All who sat in the council, looking steadfastly (staring) at Stephen, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.

verses.text: Then the high priest said: Are these things so?
Stephen said: Men, brothers, and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Charran (Haran).
God said to Abraham: Get out of your country, and from your family, and come into the land which I will show you.
Then Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, and lived in Charran (Haran). From there, when his father was dead, God moved him into this land, where you now live.

God gave Abraham no inheritance in it, no, not even enough to set his foot on. Yet God promised that He would give it to him for a possession, and to his seed (family line) after him, when as yet he had no child.
God spoke this way: That his seed (family line) should live as strangers in a foreign land. The people there would bring them into bondage (slavery), and treat them badly 400 years.
And the nation to whom they will be in bondage (slavery) I will judge, said God. After that they will come out, and serve Me in this place.

God gave Abraham the agreement of circumcision (cutting off the foreskin). So Abraham became the father of Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob. And Jacob became the father of the 12 patriarchs (fathers of the tribes).
The patriarchs (fathers of the tribes), moved with envy (jealousy), sold Joseph into Egypt. But God was with Joseph,
And delivered (rescued) Joseph out of all his afflictions (troubles). God gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh made Joseph governor over Egypt and all his house.
Now there came a dearth (famine) over all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction (trouble). Our fathers found no sustenance (food).
But when Jacob heard that there was corn (grain) in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.
At the second time Joseph was made known to his brothers. And Joseph's family was made known to Pharaoh.
Then Joseph sent and called his father Jacob to him, and all his family, 75 souls (people).
So Jacob went down into Egypt, and died, he and our fathers,
And they were carried over into Sychem (Shechem), and laid in the sepulchre (tomb) that Abraham bought for a sum of money from the sons of Emmor (Hamor) the father of Sychem.
But when the time of the promise came near, which God had sworn (promised with an oath) to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
Until another king arose, who did not know Joseph.
This king dealt subtly (with tricks) with our family, and treated our fathers badly. He made them cast out (leave outside) their young children, so that the babies would not live.
In that time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair (very beautiful) to God. He was nourished (cared for) in his father's house 3 months.
When Moses was cast out (left outside), Pharaoh's daughter took him up, and nourished (raised) him as her own son.
Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.
When Moses was 40 years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
Seeing one of them suffer wrong, Moses defended him, and avenged (paid back) the one who was oppressed (treated cruelly), and struck the Egyptian.
For Moses supposed (thought) his brothers would have understood how God by his hand would deliver (rescue) them. But they did not understand.
The next day Moses showed himself to 2 of them as they fought. He would have set them at one (at peace) again, saying: Sirs, you are brothers. Why do you do wrong to one another?
But the one who did his neighbor wrong thrust Moses away, saying: Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
Will you kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?
Then Moses fled at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian (Midian). There he became the father of 2 sons.
When 40 years were finished, there appeared to Moses in the wilderness (desert) of mount Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight. As he came near to look at it, the voice of the Lord came to him,
Saying: I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and dared not look.
Then the Lord said to him: Take off your shoes from your feet. For the place where you stand is holy ground.
I have seen, I have seen the affliction (suffering) of My people who are in Egypt. I have heard their groaning, and have come down to deliver (rescue) them. And now come, I will send you into Egypt.
This Moses whom they refused, saying: Who made you a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer (rescuer) by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
Moses brought them out, after he had shown wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness (desert) 40 years.
This is that Moses, who said to the children of Israel: A Prophet the Lord your God will raise up to you from your brothers, like me. Him you will hear.

This is Moses, who was in the church (gathering of God's people) in the wilderness (desert) with the angel who spoke to him in mount Sinai, and with our fathers. Moses received the lively oracles (living words of God) to give to us.
Our fathers would not obey Moses, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt.
They said to Aaron: Make us gods to go before us. For as for this Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not (do not know) what has become of him.
They made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

Then God turned, and gave them up to worship the host (army) of heaven (the sun, moon, and stars), as it is written in the book of the prophets: O house of Israel, have you offered to Me slain beasts and sacrifices by the space of 40 years in the wilderness (desert)?
Yes, you took up the tabernacle (tent) of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures (idols) which you made to worship them. And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.
Our fathers had the tabernacle (tent) of witness in the wilderness (desert), as God had appointed (ordered), speaking to Moses, that he should make it by the pattern that he had seen.
Our fathers who came after also brought it in with Jesus (Joshua) into the land of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), whom God drove out before the face of our fathers, to the days of David.
David found favor before God, and desired to find a tabernacle (dwelling place) for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon built God a house.
But the most High does not live in temples made with hands, as the prophet says:
Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. What house will you build Me? says the Lord. Or what is the place of My rest?
Has not My hand made all these things?
You stiffnecked (stubborn) and uncircumcised (unclean) in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you.

Which of the prophets have your fathers not persecuted (attacked)? They have killed those who showed before about the coming of the Just One (the Righteous One). Of Him you have now been the betrayers and murderers.
You have received the law by the disposition (order) of angels, and have not kept it.
When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on Stephen with their teeth (ground their teeth at him).
But Stephen, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up steadfastly (stared) into heaven. He saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God.
Stephen said: Look, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.
Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon Stephen with one accord (all together),
And cast him out of the city, and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man whose name was Saul.
They stoned Stephen, as he was calling upon God and saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
Stephen kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge (do not hold this sin against them). When he had said this, he fell asleep (died).

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Saul was consenting (agreeing) to Stephen's death. At that time there was a great persecution (attack) against the church which was at Jerusalem. And they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
Devout (God-fearing) men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation (crying) over him.
As for Saul, he made havoc of (tore apart) the church, entering into every house. He dragged men and women, and committed (put) them to prison.
So those who were scattered abroad went everywhere preaching the word.
Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ to them.
The people with one accord (all together) gave heed (paid attention) to the things which Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.
For unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many who were possessed with them. And many taken with palsies (who could not move their bodies), and who were lame, were healed.
There was great joy in that city.
But there was a certain man, called Simon, who before in the same city used sorcery (magic), and bewitched (amazed and fooled) the people of Samaria. He gave out that he himself was some great one.
They all gave heed (paid attention) to Simon, from the least to the greatest, saying: This man is the great power of God.
They had regard to (followed) Simon, because for a long time he had bewitched (amazed and fooled) them with sorceries (magic).
But when they believed Philip preaching the things about the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
Then Simon himself believed also. When he was baptized, he continued with Philip. He wondered, seeing the miracles and signs which were done.
When the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent to them Peter and John.
When Peter and John had come down, they prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit.
For as yet the Holy Spirit had fallen upon none of them. They were only baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Spirit was given, he offered them money,
Saying: Give me also this power, that on whoever I lay hands, they may receive the Holy Spirit.
But Peter said to Simon: Your money perish (be destroyed) with you, because you have thought that the gift of God may be bought with money.
You have neither part nor lot (share) in this matter. For your heart is not right in the sight of God.
So repent (change your heart) of this your wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness (full of bitter poison), and in the bond (chains) of iniquity (sin).
Then Simon answered and said: Pray to the Lord for me, that none of these things which you have spoken come upon me.
When Peter and John had testified (told the truth) and preached the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem. They preached the gospel (good news) in many villages of the Samaritans.
The angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying: Get up, and go toward the south, to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza, which is desert.

Philip got up and went. And look, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch (an officer who could not have children) of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians. He had the charge (care) of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem to worship.
He was returning, and sitting in his chariot he read Esaias (Isaiah) the prophet.
Then the Spirit said to Philip: Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.
Philip ran there to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias (Isaiah). Philip said: Do you understand what you are reading?
The eunuch said: How can I, unless some man should guide me? And he asked Philip to come up and sit with him.
The place of the scripture which he read was this: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter. And like a lamb is silent before his shearer (the man who cuts its wool), so He did not open His mouth.
In His humiliation (shame) His judgment was taken away. And who will declare (tell about) His generation (family line)? For His life is taken from the earth.
The eunuch answered Philip, and said: I pray you, about whom does the prophet say this? About himself, or about some other man?
Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached Jesus to him.
As they went on their way, they came to some water. The eunuch said: Look, here is water. What hinders (stops) me from being baptized?
Philip said: If you believe with all your heart, you may. The eunuch answered and said: I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
He commanded the chariot to stand still. They went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, so that the eunuch saw him no more. And he went on his way rejoicing.
But Philip was found at Azotus. Passing through, he preached in all the cities, until he came to Caesarea.

verses.text: Saul was still breathing out threatenings and slaughter (threats to kill) against the disciples of the Lord. He went to the high priest,
And asked him for letters to the synagogues (meeting houses) at Damascus. If Saul found any of this way (followers of Jesus), whether men or women, he could bring them bound (tied up) to Jerusalem.
As Saul traveled, he came near Damascus. And suddenly a light from heaven shined round about (all around) him.
Saul fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying to him: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting (attacking) Me?
Saul said: Who are You, Lord? And the Lord said: I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting (attacking). It is hard for you to kick against the pricks (to fight against Me).
Saul, trembling and astonished (amazed), said: Lord, what do You want me to do? And the Lord said to him: Arise (get up), and go into the city, and it will be told you what you must do.
The men who traveled with Saul stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.
Saul got up from the earth. When his eyes were opened, he saw no man. But they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
Saul was 3 days without sight, and he did not eat or drink.
There was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision: Ananias. And Ananias said: Look, I am here, Lord.
The Lord said to Ananias: Arise (get up), and go into the street which is called Straight. Ask in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus. For look, he is praying,
And has seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, so that he might receive his sight.
Then Ananias answered: Lord, I have heard from many people about this man, how much evil he has done to Your saints (holy people) at Jerusalem.
And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind (arrest) all who call on Your name.
But the Lord said to Ananias: Go your way. For Saul is a chosen vessel (tool) unto Me, to bear (carry) My name before the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and kings, and the children of Israel.
For I will show Saul how great things he must suffer for My name's sake.

Ananias went his way, and entered into the house. Putting his hands on Saul, he said: Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you came, has sent me. He sent me so that you might receive your sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
Right away there fell from Saul's eyes something like scales. He received sight forthwith (at once), and got up, and was baptized.
When Saul had received meat (food), he was strengthened. Then Saul was certain days (some days) with the disciples who were at Damascus.
Straightway (right away) Saul preached Christ in the synagogues (meeting houses), that He is the Son of God.

But all who heard Saul were amazed, and said: Is not this the man who destroyed those who called on this name in Jerusalem? Did he not come here for that intent (purpose), to bring them bound (tied up) to the chief priests?
But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded (confused) the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the very Christ.
After many days were fulfilled (had passed), the Jews took counsel (made plans) to kill Saul.
But their laying await (plan to hide and attack) was known by Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.
Then the disciples took Saul by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.
When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he assayed (tried) to join himself to the disciples. But they were all afraid of him, and did not believe that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took Saul, and brought him to the apostles. Barnabas told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, and that the Lord had spoken to him. And he told how Saul had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.
Saul was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.
Saul spoke boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed (argued) against the Grecians (Greek-speaking Jews). But they went about to slay (tried to kill) him.
When the brothers knew this, they brought Saul down to Caesarea, and sent him away to Tarsus.

Then the churches had rest throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified (built up). Walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, they were multiplied (grew in number).
It came to pass, as Peter passed through all parts of the land, he came down also to the saints (holy people) who lived at Lydda.
There Peter found a certain man named Aeneas, who had kept his bed 8 years, and was sick of the palsy (could not move his body).
Peter said to him: Aeneas, Jesus Christ makes you whole (healed). Arise (get up), and make your bed. And Aeneas got up right away.
All who lived at Lydda and Saron (Sharon) saw him, and turned to the Lord.
Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and almsdeeds (gifts to the poor) which she did.
It came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died. When they had washed her body, they laid her in an upper room.
Lydda was nigh (near) to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there. So they sent to him 2 men, asking him not to delay to come to them.

Then Peter got up and went with them. When he came, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping. They showed the coats and clothes which Dorcas made while she was with them.
But Peter put them all outside, and kneeled down, and prayed. Turning to the body, Peter said: Tabitha, arise (get up). And she opened her eyes. When she saw Peter, she sat up.
Peter gave her his hand, and lifted her up. When he had called the saints (holy people) and widows, he presented her alive.
It was known throughout all Joppa. And many believed in the Lord.
It came to pass that Peter tarried (stayed) many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner (a man who made leather).

verses.text: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion (army officer over 100 soldiers) of the band (group of soldiers) called the Italian band.
Cornelius was a devout (God-fearing) man, and one who feared God with all his house. He gave much alms (gifts to the poor) to the people, and prayed to God always.
Cornelius saw in a vision evidently (clearly), about the ninth hour of the day (3 in the afternoon), an angel of God coming in to him, and saying to him: Cornelius.

When Cornelius looked at the angel, he was afraid, and said: What is it, Lord? And the angel said to him: Your prayers and your alms (gifts to the poor) have come up for a memorial (a reminder) before God.
And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname (other name) is Peter.
He lodges (stays) with one Simon a tanner (a man who made leather), whose house is by the sea side. Peter will tell you what you ought to do.
When the angel who spoke to Cornelius had left, Cornelius called 2 of his household servants, and a devout (God-fearing) soldier from those who waited on him continually.
When Cornelius had told them all these things, he sent them to Joppa.
On the next day, as they went on their journey and came near the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray about the sixth hour (noon).
Peter became very hungry, and would have eaten. But while they made the food ready, he fell into a trance (a vision from God).
Peter saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel (container) coming down to him, like a great sheet knit (tied) at the 4 corners, and let down to the earth.
In it were all kinds of fourfooted beasts (animals with 4 legs) of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls (birds) of the air.
There came a voice to Peter: Rise (get up), Peter. Kill, and eat.
But Peter said: Not so, Lord. For I have never eaten anything that is common (not holy) or unclean.
The voice spoke to Peter again the second time: What God has cleansed (made clean), do not call common (not holy).
This was done 3 times. And the vessel (container) was received up again into heaven.
Peter doubted (wondered) in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean. Look, the men who were sent from Cornelius had asked for Simon's house, and stood before the gate,
And called, and asked whether Simon, who was surnamed (also named) Peter, was lodging (staying) there.
While Peter thought about the vision, the Spirit said to him: Look, 3 men are looking for you.
So arise (get up), and go down, and go with them, doubting nothing. For I have sent them.
Then Peter went down to the men who were sent to him from Cornelius, and said: Look, I am the one you are looking for. What is the cause why you have come?

They said: Cornelius the centurion (army officer), a just (good and fair) man, and one who fears God, and has a good report (name) among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by a holy angel. The angel told him to send for you to come to his house, and to hear words from you.
Then Peter called them in, and lodged them (let them stay the night). On the next day Peter went away with them. And some brothers from Joppa went with him.
The next day they entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, and had called together his relatives and close friends.
As Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him.
But Peter took him up, saying: Stand up. I myself also am a man.
As Peter talked with Cornelius, he went in, and found many who had come together.

Peter said to them: You know how it is an unlawful thing (against our law) for a man who is a Jew to keep company, or come to one of another nation. But God has shown me that I should not call any man common (not holy) or unclean.
So I came to you without gainsaying (arguing), as soon as I was sent for. So I ask, for what intent (reason) have you sent for me?
Cornelius said: 4 days ago I was fasting (going without food) until this hour. At the ninth hour (3 in the afternoon) I prayed in my house. And look, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
And said: Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your alms (gifts to the poor) are had in remembrance (remembered) in the sight of God.

So send to Joppa, and call here Simon, whose surname (other name) is Peter. He is lodging (staying) in the house of one Simon a tanner (a man who made leather) by the sea side. When he comes, he will speak to you.
So right away I sent to you. And you have done well that you have come. Now we are all here present before God, to hear all things that God has commanded you.
Then Peter opened his mouth, and said: Of a truth (truly) I perceive (understand) that God is no respecter of persons (does not show favor to some people over others).
But in every nation, the one who fears God, and works righteousness (does what is right), is accepted with Him.
The word which God sent to the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ. He is Lord of all.
That word, I say, you know, which was published (told) throughout all Judea, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached.
You know how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power. Jesus went about doing good, and healing all who were oppressed (held down) by the devil. For God was with Jesus.
And we are witnesses of all things which Jesus did both in the land of the Jews, and in Jerusalem. They killed Him and hanged Him on a tree.
God raised Jesus up the third day, and showed Him openly,
Not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen before by God, even to us, who ate and drank with Jesus after He rose from the dead.
Jesus commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify (tell the truth) that it is He who was ordained (chosen) by God to be the Judge of the living and the dead.
To Jesus all the prophets give witness, that through His name whoever believes in Him will receive remission (forgiveness) of sins.
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the word.

Those of the circumcision (Jewish believers) who believed were astonished (amazed), as many as came with Peter. They were amazed because on the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) also was poured out the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For they heard them speak with tongues (languages), and magnify (praise) God. Then Peter answered:
Can any man forbid (stop) water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as well as we?
Peter commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they asked Peter to tarry (stay) certain days (some days).

10.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: The apostles and brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) had also received the word of God.
When Peter had come up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision (Jewish believers) contended (argued) with him,
Saying: You went in to men uncircumcised (not Jews), and ate with them.
But Peter told the matter from the beginning, and explained it to them in order, saying:

I was in the city of Joppa praying. In a trance (a vision from God) I saw a vision. A certain vessel (container) came down, like a great sheet, let down from heaven by 4 corners. And it came even to me.
When I had fastened my eyes on it, I considered (looked closely), and saw fourfooted beasts (animals with 4 legs) of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls (birds) of the air.
I heard a voice saying to me: Arise (get up), Peter. Kill and eat.
But I said: Not so, Lord. For nothing common (not holy) or unclean has at any time entered into my mouth.
But the voice answered me again from heaven: What God has cleansed (made clean), do not call common (not holy).
This was done 3 times. And all were drawn up again into heaven.
And look, right away there were 3 men already come to the house where I was, sent from Caesarea to me.
The Spirit told me to go with them, nothing doubting. Also these 6 brothers went with me, and we entered into the man's house.
He showed us how he had seen an angel in his house. The angel stood and said to him: Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, whose surname (other name) is Peter.
He will tell you words, by which you and all your house will be saved.
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, as on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how He said: John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
So God gave them the same gift as He did to us, who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ. What was I, that I could withstand (stand against) God?

When they heard these things, they held their peace (were quiet), and glorified (praised) God, saying: Then God has also granted (given) to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) repentance (a change of heart) unto life.

Now those who were scattered abroad because of the persecution (attack) that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phenice (Phoenicia), and Cyprus, and Antioch. They preached the word to no one but to the Jews only.
Some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene. When they had come to Antioch, they spoke to the Grecians (Greek-speaking people), preaching the Lord Jesus.
The hand of the Lord was with them. And a great number believed, and turned to the Lord.
Then news of these things came to the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem. And they sent out Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch.
When Barnabas came, and had seen the grace of God, he was glad. He exhorted (encouraged) them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave (hold on) to the Lord.
For Barnabas was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And many people were added to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went away to Tarsus, to look for Saul.
When Barnabas had found Saul, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they gathered with the church, and taught many people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
In these days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them named Agabus stood up, and signified (showed) by the Spirit that there would be great dearth (famine) throughout all the world. This came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar.
Then the disciples, each one according to their ability, decided to send relief (help) to the brothers who lived in Judea.
They also did this, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

11.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now about that time Herod the king stretched out his hands to vex (hurt) certain people of the church.
Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword.
Because Herod saw that it pleased the Jews, he went further to take Peter also. Then were the days of unleavened bread (the feast of bread made without yeast).
When Herod had taken Peter, he put him in prison. He gave Peter to 4 quaternions (groups of 4 soldiers) to keep him. Herod intended after Easter (the Passover) to bring Peter out to the people.
So Peter was kept in prison. But prayer was made without ceasing (stopping) by the church to God for him.
When Herod would have brought Peter out, the same night Peter was sleeping between 2 soldiers, bound (tied) with 2 chains. And the keepers (guards) before the door kept the prison.

And look, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison. The angel struck Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying: Arise up (get up) quickly. And Peter's chains fell off from his hands.
The angel said to Peter: Gird yourself (put on your belt), and tie on your sandals. And Peter did so. The angel said to him: Put your garment (coat) around you, and follow me.
Peter went out, and followed the angel. Peter did not know that it was true which was done by the angel, but thought he saw a vision.

When they were past the first and the second ward (guard), they came to the iron gate that leads to the city. It opened to them by itself. They went out, and passed on through one street. And right away the angel departed from Peter.

When Peter had come to himself, he said: Now I know for sure, that the Lord has sent His angel. The Lord has delivered (rescued) me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation (what they hoped would happen) of the people of the Jews.
When Peter had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname (other name) was Mark. Many were gathered together there praying.
As Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel (young girl) came to hearken (listen), named Rhoda.
When Rhoda knew Peter's voice, she did not open the gate for gladness. But she ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
They said to her: You are mad (out of your mind). But she constantly affirmed (kept saying) that it was even so. Then they said: It is his angel.
But Peter kept on knocking. When they had opened the door, and saw him, they were astonished (amazed).

Peter, beckoning (waving) to them with his hand to hold their peace (be quiet), told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And Peter said: Go show these things to James, and to the brothers. And he departed, and went into another place.
As soon as it was day, there was no small stir (trouble) among the soldiers, about what had become of Peter.
When Herod had looked for Peter, and did not find him, he examined the keepers (guards), and commanded that they should be put to death. And Herod went down from Judea to Caesarea, and stayed there.

Herod was highly displeased with the people of Tyre and Sidon. But they came with one accord (all together) to him. They made Blastus, the king's chamberlain (personal servant), their friend, and desired (asked for) peace. For their country was nourished (fed) by the king's country.
On a set day Herod, dressed in royal clothes, sat upon his throne, and made an oration (speech) to them.
The people gave a shout, saying: It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.
Right away the angel of the Lord struck Herod, because he did not give God the glory. And he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost (died).
But the word of God grew and multiplied (spread).
Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry (work). And they took with them John, whose surname (other name) was Mark.

12.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase and was missing verse 25), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas, and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch (ruler), and Saul.
As they ministered (served) to the Lord, and fasted (went without food), the Holy Spirit said: Separate (set apart) Barnabas and Saul for Me, for the work which I have called them to do.
When they had fasted (gone without food) and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
So they, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.
When they were at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues (meeting houses) of the Jews. And they also had John to minister (help) them.
When they had gone through the isle (island) to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer (magician), a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Barjesus.
Barjesus was with the deputy (governor) of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent (wise) man. The deputy called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired (wanted) to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the sorcerer (magician), for that is what his name means, withstood (stood against) them. He tried to turn away the deputy (governor) from the faith.
Then Saul, who also is called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, set his eyes on Elymas,

And said: O full of all subtilty (tricks) and all mischief (evil), you child of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness (being right with God), will you not stop perverting (twisting) the right ways of the Lord?

And now, look, the hand of the Lord is upon you. You will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season (a while). And right away there fell on Elymas a mist and a darkness. He went about looking for someone to lead him by the hand.
Then the deputy (governor), when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished (amazed) at the doctrine (teaching) of the Lord.
Now when Paul and his company left Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia. And John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
But when Paul and Barnabas left Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia. They went into the synagogue (meeting house) on the sabbath day, and sat down.

After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue (meeting house) sent to them, saying: Men and brothers, if you have any word of exhortation (encouragement) for the people, say on.
Then Paul stood up, and beckoning (waving) with his hand said: Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.
The God of this people of Israel chose our fathers. God exalted (lifted up) the people when they lived as strangers in the land of Egypt. With a high arm (great power) God brought them out of it.
About the time of 40 years God suffered (put up with) their manners (ways) in the wilderness (desert).
When God had destroyed 7 nations in the land of Canaan, He divided their land to them by lot (a way of choosing).
After that God gave them judges about the space of 450 years, until Samuel the prophet.
Afterward they desired (asked for) a king. And God gave them Saul the son of Cis (Kish), a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for 40 years.

When God had removed Saul, He raised up David to be their king. God also gave testimony (witness) about David, and said: I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after My own heart, who will fulfil all My will.
From this man's seed (family line) God, according to His promise, has raised to Israel a Savior, Jesus.
Before Jesus came, John had first preached the baptism of repentance (a change of heart) to all the people of Israel.
As John fulfilled (finished) his course (work), he said: Who do you think I am? I am not He. But look, there comes One after me, whose shoes of His feet I am not worthy to untie.
Men and brothers, children of the family of Abraham, and whoever among you fears God, to you is the word of this salvation sent.

For those who live at Jerusalem, and their rulers, did not know Jesus, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath day. But they have fulfilled them in condemning (judging guilty) Him.
Though they found no cause of death in Jesus, yet they asked Pilate that He should be killed.
When they had fulfilled all that was written about Jesus, they took Him down from the tree, and laid Him in a sepulchre (tomb).
But God raised Jesus from the dead.
Jesus was seen many days by those who came up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are His witnesses to the people.
We declare (tell) to you glad tidings (good news), how that the promise which was made to the fathers,
God has fulfilled the same to us their children, in that He has raised up Jesus again. As it is also written in the second psalm: You are My Son, this day have I begotten (fathered) You.
About God raising Jesus up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption (decay), God said this: I will give you the sure mercies of David.
So God says also in another psalm: You will not let Your Holy One see corruption (decay).
For David, after he had served his own generation (people living then) by the will of God, fell asleep (died), and was laid with his fathers, and saw corruption (decay).
But Jesus, whom God raised again, saw no corruption (decay).
So let it be known to you, men and brothers, that through this Man (Jesus) is preached to you the forgiveness of sins.
And by Jesus all who believe are justified (made right with God) from all things, from which you could not be justified (made right with God) by the law of Moses.
So beware, so that what is spoken of in the prophets does not come upon you:
Look, you despisers (people who look down on God), and wonder, and perish (be destroyed). For I work a work in your days, a work which you will not believe, even if a man tells it to you.
When the Jews had gone out of the synagogue (meeting house), the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) asked that these words might be preached to them the next sabbath.

Now when the meeting broke up, many of the Jews and religious proselytes (people who became Jews) followed Paul and Barnabas. Paul and Barnabas, speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.
The next sabbath day almost the whole city came together to hear the word of God.
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with envy (jealousy). They spoke against the things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming (speaking against God).

Then Paul and Barnabas grew bold, and said: It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you. But seeing you put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, look, we turn to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
For so has the Lord commanded us, saying: I have set You to be a light of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), that You should be for salvation to the ends of the earth.
When the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) heard this, they were glad, and glorified (praised) the word of the Lord. And as many as were ordained (chosen) to eternal life believed.
The word of the Lord was published (spread) throughout all the region.

But the Jews stirred up the devout (God-fearing) and honorable women, and the chief men of the city. They raised persecution (attacks) against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled (threw) them out of their coasts (land).
But Paul and Barnabas shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Spirit.

13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: It came to pass in Iconium, that Paul and Barnabas went both together into the synagogue (meeting house) of the Jews. They spoke so that a great crowd both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed.
But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and made their minds evil affected (turned bad) against the brothers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed a long time speaking boldly in the Lord. The Lord gave testimony (witness) to the word of His grace, and granted (allowed) signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
But the crowd of the city was divided. Some were with the Jews, and some with the apostles.
When there was an assault (attack) made both of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and also of the Jews with their rulers, to use them despitefully (mistreat them), and to stone them,
Paul and Barnabas knew about it, and fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and to the region that lies round about (all around).
And there they preached the gospel (good news).
There sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent (weak, not able to use) in his feet. He was a cripple from his mother's womb (from birth), who had never walked.
The same man heard Paul speak. Paul, steadfastly beholding (looking closely at) him, and seeing that he had faith to be healed,
Said with a loud voice: Stand upright on your feet. And the man leaped and walked.
When the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the language of Lycaonia: The gods have come down to us in the likeness (looking like) of men.
They called Barnabas, Jupiter, and Paul, Mercurius (Mercury), because Paul was the chief speaker.
Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands (flower crowns) to the gates. He would have done sacrifice with the people.
When the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard about this, they rent (tore) their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,

And saying: Sirs, why do you do these things? We also are men of like passions (feelings) with you. We preach to you that you should turn from these vanities (empty things) to the living God, who made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are in them.
In times past God suffered (allowed) all nations to walk in their own ways.
Nevertheless God did not leave Himself without witness. For God did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
With these sayings they could hardly stop the people from doing sacrifice to them.
Then certain Jews came there from Antioch and Iconium. They persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing (thinking) he had been dead.
But as the disciples stood round about (all around) Paul, he got up, and came into the city. The next day he left with Barnabas to Derbe.
When they had preached the gospel (good news) to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,

Confirming (making strong) the souls of the disciples, and exhorting (encouraging) them to continue in the faith. They said that we must through much tribulation (trouble) enter into the kingdom of God.
When they had ordained (chosen) them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting (going without food), they commended (gave) them to the Lord, on whom they believed.
After they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
When they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia.
From there they sailed to Antioch, where they had been recommended (given) to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled (finished).
When they had come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed (told) all that God had done with them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
And there they abode (stayed) a long time with the disciples.

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Certain men who came down from Judea taught the brothers, saying: Unless you are circumcised (cut off the foreskin) after the manner (way) of Moses, you cannot be saved.

So when Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension (disagreement) and disputation (arguing) with them, they decided that Paul and Barnabas, and certain others of them, should go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.

Being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice (Phoenicia) and Samaria, declaring (telling about) the conversion (turning to God) of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). And they caused great joy to all the brothers.
When they had come to Jerusalem, they were received by the church, and by the apostles and elders. And they declared (told) all things that God had done with them.

But there rose up certain of the sect (group) of the Pharisees who believed, saying: It was needful (necessary) to circumcise (cut off the foreskin of) them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
The apostles and elders came together to consider this matter.

When there had been much disputing (arguing), Peter rose up, and said to them: Men and brothers, you know that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel (good news), and believe.
God, who knows the hearts, gave them witness (showed He accepted them), giving them the Holy Spirit, even as He did to us.
God put no difference between us and them, purifying (cleaning) their hearts by faith.
So now why do you tempt (test) God, to put a yoke (heavy load) on the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear (carry)?
But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we will be saved, even as they.
Then all the crowd kept silence, and gave audience (listened) to Barnabas and Paul. They declared (told) what miracles and wonders God had done among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) by them.
After they had held their peace (become quiet), James answered, saying: Men and brothers, listen to me.
Simeon (Peter) has declared (told) how God at the first did visit the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), to take out of them a people for His name.
The words of the prophets agree with this. As it is written:
After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle (tent) of David, which is fallen down. I will build again its ruins, and I will set it up,
So that the rest of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), upon whom My name is called, says the Lord, who does all these things.
Known unto God are all His works from the beginning of the world.
So my sentence (judgment) is, that we do not trouble those who from among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) are turned to God.
But that we write to them, that they abstain from (stay away from) pollutions of idols (things made unclean by idols), and from fornication (sexual sin), and from things strangled, and from blood.
For Moses from old time has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues (meeting houses) every sabbath day.

Then it pleased the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They sent Judas surnamed (also named) Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers.

They wrote letters by them after this manner (in this way): The apostles and elders and brothers send greeting to the brothers who are of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia.

We have heard that certain people who went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting (upsetting) your souls, saying: You must be circumcised, and keep the law. To them we gave no such commandment.
It seemed good to us, being gathered with one accord (all agreeing together), to send chosen men to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
Men who have hazarded (risked) their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we have sent Judas and Silas, who will also tell you the same things by mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay on you no greater burden (load) than these necessary things:

That you abstain from (stay away from) meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication (sexual sin). If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Fare you well (goodbye).
So when they were dismissed (sent off), they came to Antioch. When they had gathered the crowd together, they delivered (gave) the letter.
When they had read it, they rejoiced for the consolation (comfort).
Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted (encouraged) the brothers with many words, and confirmed (made them strong).
After they had stayed there a space (a while), they were let go in peace from the brothers to the apostles.
Notwithstanding (but) it pleased Silas to abide (stay) there still.
Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
Some days after, Paul said to Barnabas: Let us go again and visit our brothers in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they are doing.
Barnabas determined (decided) to take with them John, whose surname (other name) was Mark.
But Paul did not think it good to take John Mark with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and did not go with them to the work.
The contention (fighting) was so sharp between them, that they departed apart (separated) from one another. And so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed to Cyprus.
Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended (given) by the brothers to the grace of God.
Paul went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming (making strong) the churches.

15.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland roads and arrived at Ephesus. There he found some disciples
And asked them: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed? They answered: No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.
So Paul asked: Then what baptism did you receive? They replied: John's baptism.
Paul said: John's baptism was a baptism for turning from sin. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him. That is, in Jesus.
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them. They spoke in other languages and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months. He argued persuasively about the kingdom of God.

But some of them became stubborn and refused to believe. They spoke evil about the Way in front of everyone. So Paul left them and took the disciples with him. He had discussions every day in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years, so that all the Jews and Greeks who lived in the province of Asia heard the word of the Lord.
God did extraordinary miracles through Paul,
Even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul were taken to sick people. Their illnesses were healed, and evil spirits left them.
